ruled_out_vectors.vector: Forge permit with arbitrary feeOnTop (unsigned field) → drain extra tokens
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: feeOnTop is unsigned in SWAP_TYPEHASH but signer's limitAmount caps total exposure. AMM enforces limitAmount at AMMModule.sol:2208. Known low-severity, below submission threshold.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Spoof executor context → settle orders with wrong recipient
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: PermitTransferHandler.ammHandleTransfer() checks msg.sender == AMM at L115. Only AMM can call. Executor is genuine swap caller.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Replay CLOB order with different nonce context
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOBHelper.closeOrder() checks ptrOrder.maker != maker at L36. Order nonces monotonically increment via nextOrderNonce++. Cannot replay.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Redirect fee to attacker address via hook configuration

ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Cosignatures use _hashTypedDataV4 with chain-specific domain separator. PermitC domain is also chain-bound. Known CP-002 only affects destroyCosigner (universal domain, Low).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Deploy ERC-1271 contract returning true for any hash → bypass signature checks
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: from address IS the ERC-1271 contract. Attacker would only drain tokens they approved from their own contract. Self-inflicted, no victim.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Call afterSwapRefund callback directly (not via AMM)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: afterSwapRefund checks msg.sender != AMM at CLOBTransferHandler.sol:316-318. Only AMM can call.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Malicious permitProcessor that skips actual token transfer
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMM independently checks balanceInBefore + amountIn == balanceInAfter at AMMModule.sol:2207-2210. Cannot fake transfer.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Forge cross-module caller context → bypass access control
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All AMMStandardHook state-changing functions check msg.sender == AMM via _requireCallerIsAMM() at L940-943.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Reuse permit signature with different from address → drain another user's tokens
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: from is part of PermitC typehash. Changing from invalidates the EIP-712 signature. Cryptographically bound.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Partial fill ratio manipulation via rounding
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: FullMath.mulDiv truncates (rounds down), reducing maxAmountIn. This protects the signer by allowing less input, not more.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: CLOB fill rounding exploitation via dust-loop (calculateFixedInput rounds UP)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: mulDivRoundingUp at CLOBHelper.sol:313-314 rounds output UP, benefiting makers at executor's expense. Rounding direction prevents attacker extraction.
PermitC's own nonce/fill tracking prevents underlying permit replay. Cosignature binds to specific executor address. Reusable cosignature is by-design for partial fills.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: CLOB callback data manipulation → afterSwapRefund with wrong params
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Callback data constructed by CLOB handler itself (L288-293), not executor. AMM forwards it without modification. Executor cannot inject malicious callback.

theft_theses.thesis: Forge permit with arbitrary feeOnTop to drain extra tokens beyond signed amount
Use malicious permitProcessor to bypass signature verification and steal signer funds
Exploit CLOB fill rounding (mulDivRoundingUp) via many tiny fills to extract dust per iteration
